text: What is proved is about the method, not the groups: for a presentation of the shape (3.12) (paired generators with $x_i^{E_i}\in\gamma_{c-1}$, $w=\prod[x_i,x_j^{A_{ij}}]$), $w-1$ splits as in Lemma 7; $w\ne1$ forces a pair with $A_{ij}<E_iE_j$ (Lemma 9); for that pair the pairing lemma certifies the binomial error only up to $\Delta^{c+1}$ (Lemma 10) and the pairing part only up to $\Delta^{k+\min(2+\log_2 m,k)}$. So any proof of $w\in D_8$ at class 5 in this family must get two levels from relators other than the power relators of the paired generators, plus the multiplier 4 (or a cancellation between $S$ and the errors). A theorem $f_{\rm met}(5)=7$ would need an upper bound for $D_8$ that does not go through this decomposition; nothing here gives it.

text: [on paper, every step checked by computer] The identity is short. Move the scalar $128=2E_2=16E_1$ from $X_2$ onto $X_1$: $$128X_2^2X_1\equiv X_2^2\,(x_1^{128}-1),\qquad x_1^{128}=P_1^{16}=d_2^{-16}d_3^{-64}=x_5^{1024}\,d_3^{-64}\pmod{\Delta^6},$$ then $X_2^2(x_5^{1024}-1)\equiv1024X_2^2X_5\in\Delta^6$, because $512X_2^2\in\Delta^5$ (Lemma 13, a "quadratic pairing"), and $64X_2^2D_3=(64X_2)X_2D_3\in\Delta^{2+1+3}$. Only the relators of $x_1$, $x_2$, $x_5$ and class $\le4$ are used (Theorem 14). Without the carrier the same steps end in $-16X_2^2D_2$, which is $\notin\Delta^6$ [computer].

The $d_3$-part $d_3^{-64}$ is not carried: plain pairing puts it in $\Delta^{k+3}$, which is $\Delta^6$ at class 4.

text: Lemma 13 [on paper] (quadratic pairing). Let $k\in\{3,4\}$, $G$ of class $\le k+1$, $x^E=P=\prod_ld_l^{e_l}$ with $d_l\in\gamma_k$, $E=2^e\ge4$, $X=x-1$, $s\in\{0,1\}$, $2+s\le k$. Suppose that for every $l$ either $E\mid8e_l$, or $d_l^{2^{s+3}e_l}\in\gamma_{k+1+s}$. Then $2^{s+3}E\,X^2\in\Delta^{k+2+s}$.

text: Proof. $x^E-1=\sum_{m\ge1}\binom EmX^m$, so $2^{s+3}EX^2=2^{s+3}(P-1)X-\sum_{m\ge2}2^{s+3}\binom EmX^{m+1}$. Modulo $\Delta^{2k}$, $P-1\equiv\sum_le_lD_l$. A term $2^{s+3}e_lD_lX$ is $D_l\cdot\frac{8e_l}E\,(2^sEX)\in\Delta^{k+2+s}$ in the first case (pairing lemma of §6.7: $2^sEX\in\Delta^{2+s}$), and $(d_l^{2^{s+3}e_l}-1)X\in\Delta^{k+2+s}$ up to $\Delta^{2k}$ in the second. For $m=2$: $2^{s+2}E(E-1)X^3$ is $(4EX)X^2\in\Delta^{\min(4,k)+2}=\Delta^{k+2}$ for $s=0$ and $(E-1)X(8EX^2)\in\Delta^{k+3}$ for $s=1$ (by $s=0$). For $m\ge3$, $v_2\binom Em=e-v_2(m)$, so the term is a unit times $(2^{s+3-v_2(m)}EX)X^m$, of level $\ge\min(2+\max(0,s+3-v_2(m)),k)+m\ge k+2+s$. $\square$

text: Lemma 15 [on paper] (where $w$ lives). Let $G$ have class $c=k+1$, $x_i^{E_i}=P_i\in\gamma_k$, $E_j\mid A_{ij}$, and $g_1\in(\gamma_k)^{E_1}\gamma_c$, $g_2\in(\gamma_k)^{E_2}\gamma_c$ (the pairing with multiplier 1). Then $$w=[x_2,x_1^{A_{12}}]=\prod_l[x_2,d_l]^{-a_lA_{12}/E_1}\qquad(P_1=\textstyle\prod_ld_l^{-a_l}).$$ Proof. For $y,z\in\gamma_k$, $[x_i,yz]=[x_i,y][x_i,z]$ and $[x_i,y^{E_i}]=[x_i^{E_i},y]=[P_i,y]=1$ ($[x_i,y]$ is central, $\gamma_k$ is abelian). So $u_{12}u_{13}=[x_1,g_1]=1$ and $u_{23}=[x_2,h_{23}]=[x_2,g_2][x_2,h_{21}]^{-1}=[x_2,x_1^{A_{12}}]$. $\square$
